scholarships.title: Young Leaders Program (YLP) Students - Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship
scholarships.official_source: MEXT (Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology)

existing.description: Young Leaders Program (YLP) Students is the seventh type of the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship. It funds a one-year master's course at a Japanese graduate school for university or college graduates with practical work experience and for young public administrators who are expected to play an active role in Asia and other countries. The scholarship pays JPY 242,000 per month, the tuition is exempted, and round-trip airfare to and from Japan is provided. Unlike the other six MEXT scholarship types, YLP is neither embassy-recommended nor university-recommended: recruitment is conducted by the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations, the initial selection is by document screening, interview and essay writing, and the final selection is made by the YLP Committee set in MEXT.
eligibility: Under 40 years of age in principle
University or college graduate with practical work experience
Young public administrator or similar early-career leader expected to play an active role in Asia and other countries
Nominated through an official overseas recommending organisation to the embassy of Japan in a target country
Admitted to, or placed in, a master's course at a Japanese graduate school
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be under 40 years of age in principle, and must be university or college graduates with practical work experience, or young public administrators, who are expected to play an active role in Asia and other countries. The programme leads to a master's course at a Japanese graduate school.
benefits: Monthly scholarship allowance of JPY 242,000, the highest of the seven MEXT scholarship types
Round-trip airfare to and from Japan
One year of postgraduate study at a Japanese graduate school
coverage: One year of study at a Japanese graduate school
requirements: Candidates are recruited through the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations; this is neither the embassy-recommendation nor the university-recommendation route
The initial selection consists of document screening, an interview and essay writing
The second selection is done by the YLP Committee set in MEXT, and MEXT makes the final decision
The type and field of application can differ from country to country; applicants should check with the embassy whether there is an opening in the type and field they wish to apply for
The latest edition of the application guidelines governs where its contents differ from the portal's summary
documents: Application documents specified by the embassy of Japan in the target country
Recommendation from an official overseas recommending organisation
Evidence of university or college graduation
Documents required for admission to the master's course at the Japanese graduate school
existing.english_requirement: The programme leads to a master's course at a Japanese graduate school. MEXT's official portal lists Japanese language or Japanese culture training only for the Japanese studies students category; for YLP no MEXT-level examination subject is listed in the embassy-recommendation examination table, because YLP is not embassy-recommended. Language requirements therefore come from the target graduate school and the recruiting embassy.
application_method: Obtain a recommendation from an official overseas recommending organisation in your country
Register with the embassy of Japan in the target country, which conducts the initial screening
Undergo document screening, an interview and essay writing at the embassy
Have your name submitted to MEXT, whose YLP Committee conducts the second selection
Await MEXT's final decision and the placement in a master's course at a Japanese graduate school
existing.selection_notes: The initial selection is by the embassy through document screening, interview and essay writing; the subjects of any written component vary by country and region. Candidates who pass are recommended to MEXT, and the second selection is made by the YLP Committee set in MEXT, which makes the final decision.
existing.best_fit: University or college graduates under 40 with practical work experience, and young public administrators from YLP target countries in Asia and elsewhere, who can obtain a recommendation from an official overseas recommending organisation.
existing.notes: YLP is the only one of the seven MEXT scholarship types that is neither embassy-recommended nor university-recommended; the portal footnotes this as 'Recommendations from official overseas recommending organizations'. No preliminary Japanese language training is provided for this category.
existing.application_period: Not published centrally. Recruitment runs through the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations, at timings that differ by country and region.
existing.deadline_display: No central MEXT or portal deadline is published. Recruitment is conducted through the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations, so the timetable is set country by country and by the recommending organisation. Applicants must check the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their own country.

scholarships.title: JASSO Reservation Program for Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students by Pre-arrival Admission
scholarships.degree: Bachelor's, Master's, PhD, Other (junior college, college of technology 3rd year or above, specialized training college course)

existing.description: JASSO's reservation programme for the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students, for students who have already received pre-arrival admission to a Japanese institution and face financial difficulties. It pays a monthly stipend of JPY 48,000 for 12 months if the student enrols in April, or for 6 months if the student enrols in September or October. Applications are not made to JASSO directly; the applicant must apply through the school they plan to enrol in. There are three reservation categories: graduate level, EJU exam, and English courses.
eligibility: Privately-financed international student (not a Japanese Government MEXT Scholarship holder)
Has received pre-arrival admission to an eligible school listed by JASSO for the relevant reservation category
Plans to enrol as a full-time student; research students, trainees, non-degree students, advanced course students, special course students, auditing students and special students are excluded
Graduate level reservation: enrolling in a graduate school in Japan in April, or September/October for autumn enrolment

EJU exam or English courses reservation: enrolling in an undergraduate school, junior college, college of technology (3rd grade or upper) or specialized course in a specialized training college in Japan in April, or September/October for autumn enrolment
Faces financial difficulties and has an excellent academic and character record
existing.eligibility_summary: Privately-financed international students planning to enrol as full-time students in Japan using pre-arrival admission, either on the graduate level reservation, the EJU exam reservation, or the English courses reservation, and who face financial difficulties. Research students, trainees, non-degree students, advanced course students, special course students, auditing students and special students are excluded from the 'full-time student' definition for this programme.
benefits: 12 months of support for April enrollees
6 months of support for September or October enrollees
coverage: 12 months of support for April enrollees
6 months of support for September or October enrollees
requirements: JASSO does not accept applications directly from students; the procedure must be completed through the school
The school must be on the eligible list for the relevant reservation category for that enrolment cycle

For the EJU exam category JASSO uses the registered-school list as of 1 October 2025 for spring enrolment and as of 1 April 2026 for September or October enrolment, which may differ from the list published on the web page
The student must enrol as a full-time student; research students, trainees, non-degree students, advanced course students, special course students, auditing students and special students are excluded
documents: Application submitted through the school the applicant plans to enrol in, not to JASSO
Pre-arrival admission confirmation from that school
Academic and character records required by the school
Documents listed by the school for its scholarship nomination
existing.english_requirement: No language test is set by JASSO for this programme. The English courses reservation category is restricted to schools whose relevant undergraduate courses award a degree or associate degree with classes conducted only in English, so English-medium study is a feature of that category rather than a test requirement.
application_method: Obtain pre-arrival admission from a school listed as eligible for the reservation category you are applying under
Ask that school to run the scholarship nomination for the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship reservation programme
Complete the school's internal scholarship application and supporting documents
The school submits the nomination to JASSO
Receive the stipend from enrolment, for the period stated for your enrolment month
existing.selection_notes: JASSO's stated objectives for the reservation programme are to ease students' financial concerns about arrival and studies in Japan, promote pre-arrival admission and improve the level of learning. The award targets privately-financed international students with excellent academic and character records who face financial difficulties, and the practical selection is carried out through the school.
existing.best_fit: Internationally financed students who already hold pre-arrival admission from a JASSO-listed Japanese school and need help with the cost of arriving and studying in Japan.
existing.notes: The stipend is JPY 48,000 per month and JASSO states the amount may change from one academic year to another. This is a stipend only: JASSO's page lists no tuition waiver, so tuition and other living costs remain the student's responsibility.
existing.duration: 12 months for students enrolled in April (April of the year of enrolment to the following March); 6 months for students enrolled in September or October (October of the year of enrolment to the following March)
existing.application_period: School-by-school, twice a year, matching the Japanese enrolment cycles: spring enrolment (April) and autumn enrolment (September or October). JASSO publishes the eligible school and department lists for each cycle; for 2026 the autumn lists were published in June 2026 and the spring lists in January 2026.
existing.deadline_display: No JASSO deadline is published. Applications are handled entirely through the school the applicant plans to enrol in, so the deadline is the school's own pre-arrival admission and scholarship nomination deadline.
existing.program_type: Reservation programme for the MEXT Honors Scholarship, by pre-arrival admission
